title: India secures 4,700MW in Nepal, but little progress on projects - The Kathmandu Post
description: India secures 4,700MW in Nepal, but little progress on projects  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
In January 2024, Nepal signed an agreement with India to export 10,000 megawatts of electricity over the next 10 years. For India, a country long regarded as one of the world's major coal-dependent economies, importing electricity from Nepal is part of its broader effort to decarbonise its power grid.

For Nepal, electricity exports are expected to generate substantial revenue and help narrow its ballooning trade deficit with India. Industry insiders view the arrangement as a win-win for both countries. Nepal has awarded several hydropower projects to Indian developers, some through negotiated agreements, while Indian energy giants have secured major investments. Nepal is also expanding cross-border transmission infrastructure to facilitate electricity trade.

Yet the projected gains are far from guaranteed.

Among the Indian government-owned and private companies that have secured seven major hydropower projects in Nepal, with a combined capacity of around 4,700 megawatts, only one project is currently under construction.

The delays in starting construction raise questions about Nepal's ability to capitalise on its electricity export potential within the agreed timeframe. They are also likely to push back the revenue Nepal expects to earn from electricity exports.

But former energy secretary Anup Upadhyay says the delays should not be viewed solely as a lack of initiative on the part of developers. Government agencies responsible for facilitating the projects have also failed to complete necessary decisions and procedures on time, he says.

Hydropower diplomacy and India's growing footprint

In April 2023, weeks ahead of a proposed visit to India by then prime minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal, the Investment Board Nepal offered the 669MW Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project to the southern neighbour through a negotiated process.

The 53rd meeting of the Investment Board, chaired by the prime minister, approved an investment proposal worth Rs92.68 billion from India's state-owned Satluj Jal Vidyut Nigam (SJVN) to develop the project.

This was the third project awarded through negotiations on the Arun river, following the 900MW Arun-III, and 695MW Arun-IV hydropower projects.

Together, the three projects are expected to generate nearly 2,300 megawatts of electricity from the Arun river in Sankhuwasabha district.

The Investment Board and SJVN signed an agreement to develop the Arun-III hydropower project in November 2014. Nepal is expected to receive Rs348 billion over 25 years from the project. The developer will also provide Nepal 21.9 percent of the electricity worth an estimated Rs155 billion free of cost, along with another Rs107 billion in royalties.

In May 2022, Kulman Ghising, then managing director of the Nepal Electricity Authority, and Nandalal Sharma, then chairman of SJVN, signed an agreement to develop Arun-IV on behalf of their respective organisations.

Under the agreement, Nepal will receive 21.9 percent, or 152 megawatts, of the electricity generated by Arun-IV free of cost.

In July 2021, Nepal also signed a deal with SJVN to develop the 679MW Lower Arun project.

The Lower Arun project will not have a reservoir or dam. Instead, it will be developed as a tailrace project of Arun-III, allowing water discharged from the latter's powerhouse to be used for electricity generation at Lower Arun.

SJVN aims to develop projects with a combined capacity of 5,000 megawatts in Nepal by 2030.

Before the Gen Z movement in September 2025, which triggered violent protests against a political system plagued by corruption and scandals, hydropower diplomacy with India and China had also served as a tool for Nepali politicians to maintain cordial relations with New Delhi and Beijing.

Successive governments repeatedly shifted their diplomatic focus between the two neighbours, seeking to woo New Delhi or Beijing depending on the political circumstances.

In August 2022, Nepal formally awarded the much-touted West Seti Hydropower Project and Seti River-6 project in western Nepal to India through a negotiated process, nearly four years after China withdrew from the projects.

The Investment Board signed a memorandum of understanding with India's state-owned NHPC Limited to develop the two joint-storage projects, West Seti and Seti River-6, with a combined capacity of 1,250 megawatts. Here ‘joint-storage projects’ means they are being planned, studied, and developed as an interconnected, coordinated ecosystem.

India is Nepal's principal buyer of electricity. Indian companies are also developing several of the country's major hydropower projects. More importantly, India determines which projects are permitted to sell electricity across the border.

In January 2022, India's Central Electricity Authority issued the Procedure for Approval and Facilitation of Import/Export (Cross-Border) of Electricity by the Designated Authority. The procedure prohibits electricity trading from projects involving investment from a third country that shares a land border with India but does not have a bilateral cooperation agreement with India in the power sector.

The provision directly affects projects involving Chinese investment, meaning India will not purchase electricity generated by such projects.

India has not granted Nepal permission to export electricity from projects in which Chinese companies secured construction contracts through international competitive bidding. The 456MW Tamakoshi Hydropower Project, Nepal's largest hydropower project, is one example.

Although Indian companies secured contracts for the project's hydromechanical, electromechanical and transmission line works, a Chinese company undertook the civil construction. India has therefore not granted export approval so far.

Nepal has repeatedly raised the issue during energy mechanism meetings between the two countries, but the matter remains unresolved.

As a result, exporting electricity from projects developed by companies from other countries has become difficult.

Apart from the three projects in the Arun river basin, Indian companies have secured the 900MW Upper Karnali and the 480MW Phukot Karnali projects, the latter under the Electricity Generation Company.

Upadhyay says the court case delayed the Upper Karnali project.

The government and India's GMR signed a memorandum of understanding on January 24, 2008, for a survey of the Upper Karnali project and the development of a 300-megawatt hydropower plant. The government awarded the project to GMR under the build-own-operate-transfer model.

An international competitive bidding process was conducted, and the government selected GMR's proposal as the best. The two sides signed an MoU for project development in 2008.

On December 21, 2009, GMR applied to the Department of Electricity Development to increase the project's capacity from 300 megawatts to 900 megawatts.

After the Investment Board was established in 2011 under the Investment Board Act, 2011, the project was brought under the board following a Cabinet decision. The Investment Board and GMR signed the project development agreement on September 19, 2014.

However, the project remained stalled for years over several issues, including financial closure.

A meeting of the Investment Board's 68th meeting, held last month, decided to facilitate the immediate commencement of construction in accordance with the project development agreement.

This means the developer's documents submitted for financial closure have been accepted, allowing it to move ahead with the construction process.

GMR had submitted the documents on January 15, 2025.

The company had presented a letter to the Investment Board Office showing a positive response for a loan of INR65 billion from the Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA) and an in-principle agreement for Rs20 billion from a consortium of Nepali banks.

The board accepted these documents and cleared the way for construction to move forward.

Initially, GMR held a 73 percent stake in the project, while the Nepal Electricity Authority held 27 percent. To mobilise investment, GMR has also brought IREDA and SJVN into the shareholding structure.

The Investment Board's 60th meeting had already approved a revised shareholding structure under which GMR and SJVN would each hold 34 percent, IREDA 5 percent and the NEA 27 percent.

Under the project development agreement, Nepal will receive 12 percent of the electricity generated by the project free of cost.

The dam of the 456MW Upper Tamakoshi Hydropower Project, Nepal’s largest, in Dolakha. Post File Photo

Transmission lines advance as projects remain stalled

Despite delays in hydropower projects, work on cross-border transmission infrastructure between Nepal and India has been progressing.

Electricity is currently being imported and exported through the 400kV Dhalkebar-Muzaffarpur transmission line, which has a capacity of 1,000 megawatts, as well as other 132kV transmission lines.

The two countries have already agreed to increase the import capacity to 1,400 megawatts and the export capacity to 1,650 megawatts through the under-construction 400kV Dhalkebar-Sitamarhi transmission line. The line will evacuate electricity from the Dhalkebar-Muzaffarpur corridor and the Arun-III project.

Construction of the Nepal section of the Butwal-Gorakhpur transmission line is targeted for completion by next August, while the substation is expected to be completed by December 2027.

A Nepal-India secretary-level meeting has decided to advance the project with an initial capacity to import up to 130 megawatts and export up to 200 megawatts.

The combined export capacity of the two transmission lines will reach around 1,850 megawatts—1,650 megawatts through Dhalkebar-Sitamarhi and 200 megawatts through Butwal-Gorakhpur.

In addition, the new Butwal-Gorakhpur cross-border transmission line is under construction. The two countries have agreed to initially allow electricity imports of up to 130 megawatts and exports of up to 200 megawatts through the line.

According to the Ministry of Energy, efforts are also being accelerated to advance the construction of the 400kV Inaruwa-New Purnea and Dododhara (New Lamki)-Bareilly cross-border transmission lines.

The Indian companies that have secured these hydropower projects will also be responsible for finding markets for the electricity they generate. Therefore, India will be the principal market for their power.

However, the 10,000MW electricity export agreement between Nepal and India does not specify whether electricity generated by these particular projects will be exported under the agreement.

Once the projects come into operation, the Nepal government will benefit from free electricity, royalties, and other benefits.

Former energy minister Pampha Bhusal says there has long been dissatisfaction on the Nepali side that India has secured major hydropower projects in Nepal but has failed to make progress on their construction.

She says she raised the issue with Indian officials and urged them to prioritise the projects.

"Arun-III was already under construction before I became minister. During my tenure, we emphasised policy decisions, including those related to land, to ensure that it was completed by 2026. Now, I hear that completion has been pushed back to 2028," she said. "The incumbent authorities should be asked what policy or technical issues have stalled projects such as Lower Arun and Upper Karnali."

Arun-III advances, but deadlines keep slipping

Among the projects awarded to Indian companies, the 900MW Arun-III Hydropower Project is currently under construction.

The project is being developed by SJVN Arun-3 Power Development Company, a subsidiary of India's state-owned SJVN Limited. So far, 77.5 percent of the power generation component and 60 percent of the transmission line component have been completed.

Construction began in 2018, with a target of completing the project within five years. However, the deadline has been repeatedly extended due to factors including the Covid pandemic.

The project was initially scheduled to begin commercial production by mid-April 2025. Its latest completion deadline has been pushed back to mid-March 2028.

The total estimated cost of the project is Rs144 billion.

Alongside the hydropower project, a 253-kilometre-long 400kV cross-border transmission line connecting the powerhouse to Sitamarhi in India is also under construction.

The developer has already signed an agreement with India's state-owned Damodar Valley Corporation to sell 200 megawatts of electricity generated by the Arun-III project.

Nepal will receive 21.9 percent of the electricity generated by the project free of cost.

In addition, the government will receive a capacity royalty of Rs400 per kilowatt and an energy royalty of 7.5 percent for the first 15 years of electricity generation. After 15 years, the capacity royalty will increase to Rs1,800 per kilowatt and the energy royalty to 12 percent.

The 490MW Arun-4 is a semi-reservoir-type hydropower project to be developed in Sankhuwasabha district.

The project was planned to move forward under a memorandum of understanding signed between the Nepal Electricity Authority and SJVN on May 16, 2022.

Its estimated cost is Rs79.12 billion.

According to NEA Managing Director Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha, the memorandum of understanding has expired, and the process of extending its validity has been initiated .

The project will be developed by a joint venture company established by the NEA and SJVN, with the two partners holding 49 percent and 51 percent shares, respectively.

Nepal will get 21.9 percent of the electricity generated free of cost.

A project development agreement for Arun-4 is yet to be signed.

The 679MW Lower Arun project was awarded to SJVN through competitive bidding on January 29, 2021.

A memorandum of understanding was signed on July 11, 2021, followed by a project development agreement on June 1, 2023.

The estimated project cost is Rs92.67 billion.

Nepal will receive 21 percent of the electricity generated by Lower Arun free of cost.

The government will also receive a capacity royalty of Rs400 per kilowatt and an energy royalty of 7.5 percent for the first 15 years of electricity generation. After 15 years, the capacity royalty will increase to Rs1,800 per kilowatt, and the energy royalty to 12 percent.

The contract for Package 1, covering the main tunnel, spillway tunnel, adit facilities and access roads, has been awarded to Dineshchandra R Agrawal Infracon for Rs11.4921 billion.

According to India's Economic Times newspaper, Patel Engineering has secured the Package 2 contract for 15.93 billion Indian rupees. However, the project development company has not officially disclosed the contractor's details.

Investment Board spokesperson and joint secretary Bhupendra Thapa said the financial management process and construction contract procedures were being advanced simultaneously.

"The company has already acquired the land required for Lower Arun using its own funds. Financial management on the one hand and the bidding process for construction on the other are being advanced simultaneously," he said.

Financial viability and free-power disputes hold back other projects

The 900MW Upper Karnali project is being developed by GMR. The company was selected through international competitive bidding. A memorandum of understanding was signed with the company in 2008, followed by a project development agreement on September 19, 2014.

The 800MW West Seti project, initially designed for 750MW, and the 450MW Seti River-6 project have been awarded to India's state-owned National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC).

After the agreement with China Three Gorges International was terminated, the government had presented both projects for investment at the Investment Summit in March 2019. NHPC has already submitted the detailed project reports, which are currently being studied by the Investment Board.

Board spokesperson Thapa said negotiations for project development agreements were underway.

The Investment Board's 64th meeting had decided to conduct further studies on the detailed project report for West Seti.

At its meeting on September 22, 2025, the board decided to form a negotiation committee under the coordination of the Investment Board's chief executive officer. The committee was tasked with preparing a draft project development agreement and discussing the financial structure and other issues with the developer before submitting a proposal to the board.

The Investment Board has not made any further decisions since then.

West Seti is estimated to cost Rs172.51 billion, while Seti River-6 is estimated to cost Rs98.22 billion.

Under the memorandum of understanding signed between NHPC and the Investment Board Office on August 18, 2022, Nepal will receive 21.9 percent of the electricity generated by each project free of cost once commercial production begins.

However, former energy secretary Upadhyay says the financial viability of the projects must also be considered when deciding the share of free electricity Nepal should receive.

"On the one hand, Chinese companies walked away from the projects saying they were not financially viable. On the other hand, we are demanding free electricity from the same projects. We need to think about that as well. At the same time, delays in decisions by government agencies must also be examined," he said.

Pradip Rana, an adviser to NHPC, said the company had informed the government that providing free electricity from all three projects—West Seti, Seti-6 and Phukot Karnali—would make them financially unviable.

Therefore, the company has requested viability gap funding from the government.

He said no further decisions had been taken on the matter.

Rana also said the memorandums of understanding for West Seti, Seti-6 and Phukot Karnali had expired.

The 480MW Phukot Karnali project has been awarded to NHPC.

Under the memorandum of understanding signed between the Electricity Generation Company and NHPC on May 31, 2023, NHPC will hold a 51 percent stake in the joint venture company, while the Electricity Generation Company will hold the remaining 49 percent.

The project is estimated to cost Rs100 billion.

Clause 5.1 of the memorandum of understanding provides for Nepal to receive 21.9 percent of the electricity generated free of cost. However, uncertainty has emerged over the project's development after the Supreme Court last September, acting on a writ petition by two Kalikot district residents, directed the government to increase Nepal's share of free electricity.

The developer company has maintained that increasing Nepal's share could make construction difficult.

Former energy secretary Chiranjibi Chataut, meanwhile, says delays in major hydropower projects are caused by multiple factors, including investment, certainty of the electricity market and administrative sluggishness.

title: Economic Digest: A Snapshot of Nepal’s Business News - Khabarhub
description: Economic Digest: A Snapshot of Nepal’s Business News  Khabarhub

full_article:
KATHMANDU: Economic Digest presents a brief yet comprehensive roundup of major business developments in Nepal, delivered in clear and accessible summaries.

Nepal’s economic landscape presents a mixed picture, with modest stock market gains, rising gold prices, expanding investment opportunities and renewed efforts to strengthen public institutions and infrastructure. While the NEPSE index edged up marginally to 2,665.53 points, turnover increased to Rs 7.43 billion, suggesting sustained trading activity despite a larger number of declining stocks than advancing ones.

The sharp rise in Nepal Reinsurance shares following the government’s approval of additional investment highlights how policy decisions can influence investor sentiment. Meanwhile, gold prices continued to climb, reflecting divergent movements in the domestic precious metals market.

Beyond the financial sector, several government initiatives point to efforts to stimulate economic growth through structural reforms. Plans to provide subsidised loans to women entrepreneurs, promote private investment in renewable energy and expand digital public services indicate growing recognition of the need for inclusive and sustainable development. The introduction of digital systems in health insurance, aviation trade and Nepal Oil Corporation also reflects a gradual shift towards technology-driven governance and operational efficiency.

Revenue collection at Bhairahawa Customs exceeding its quarterly target offers an encouraging sign of improved trade activity. However, persistent delays in infrastructure projects remain a concern, despite the government’s move to terminate underperforming contracts and strengthen monitoring.

Tourism promotion abroad and the recovery of trekking destinations are positive developments for the service sector. Similarly, the growing interest in commercial floriculture highlights opportunities for agricultural entrepreneurship and import substitution.

Overall, these developments suggest that Nepal has opportunities to strengthen economic growth through investment, innovation and institutional reform. However, translating policy announcements into measurable outcomes, ensuring effective implementation and maintaining investor confidence will be crucial to sustaining this momentum.

NEPSE edges up 1.40 points as turnover reaches Rs 7.43 billion

The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) index posted a marginal gain of 1.40 points to close at 2,665.53 points on Wednesday, with total turnover reaching Rs 7.43 billion. The benchmark index had closed at 2,664.13 points on Tuesday after gaining 6.62 points. However, daily turnover increased from Rs 5.65 billion on Tuesday to Rs 7.43 billion on Wednesday, compared with Rs 7.18 billion on Monday. Shares of 358 companies were traded through 59,185 transactions, with 21.22 million shares changing hands. Share prices of 98 companies advanced, while 171 declined and nine remained unchanged. Nepal Reinsurance Company Limited emerged as the day’s top gainer, with its share price rising 15 percent to Rs 921.70. The surge followed Tuesday’s Cabinet approval of investment in the company’s right shares. Himalayan Reinsurance Limited also gained 11.48 percent. Swet Ganga Hydropower and Construction Limited topped the turnover chart with transactions worth Rs 858.4 million. Ghorahi Cement Limited followed with Rs 512.4 million, while Himalayan Reinsurance recorded a turnover of Rs 360.3 million. Among sectoral indices, the Others group recorded the highest gain of 6.81 percent.

Gold rises Rs 600 per tola, while silver falls Rs 20

The price of gold increased by Rs 600 per tola in the domestic market on Wednesday, while silver declined by Rs 20, according to the Federation of Nepal Gold and Silver Dealers’ Associations. Fine gold was traded at Rs 275,600 per tola on Wednesday, up from Rs 275,000 on Tuesday. In contrast, silver was priced at Rs 3,655 per tola, down from Rs 3,675 in the previous trading session. The latest movement indicates divergent price trends in the domestic precious metals market, with gold gaining value while silver recorded a decline.

Industry minister announces subsidised loans and incentives for women entrepreneurs

Minister for Industry, Commerce and Supplies Deepak Kumar Shah has announced a range of policy incentives, including collateral-free concessional loans, tax benefits and simplified technology transfer procedures, to promote women-led enterprises. Speaking at a national workshop in Lalitpur on Wednesday, Shah emphasised the need for strong government support during the initial stages of business development. Comparing startups with newborn children who require special care, he said emerging enterprises needed adequate state support to become sustainable and competitive. He announced that small and medium-sized industries registered under women entrepreneurs would be eligible for preferential startup loans at a subsidised interest rate of 3 percent. The minister also highlighted the need to address administrative hurdles and barriers to accessing finance that continue to discourage women from entering entrepreneurship. He urged government agencies and other stakeholders to work together to create an enabling environment for women-led businesses, generate employment and promote inclusive economic growth.

NRB to sell gold coins and silver medallions for Tihar

Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) will sell gold coins and silver medallions on November 5 and 6 in view of the Tihar festival. The Mint Division under the central bank’s Currency Management Department will sell the coins and medallions from its Babarmahal office between 11 am and 3 pm, subject to availability. Each customer will be allowed to purchase one 25-gram gold coin and up to two 10-gram silver medallions bearing the images of Goddess Laxmi and Lord Ganesh. Buyers must be physically present and submit a copy of their citizenship certificate, national identity card or another identification document containing their identification number. Payments can be made either in cash or through QR code. The central bank said sales would begin each day after the prices of the gold coins and silver medallions were fixed at around 11 am.

Energy minister calls for private investment to drive renewable energy growth

Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has called for greater private-sector investment to establish renewable energy as a key driver of employment generation, production and economic growth. Addressing a programme organised on Wednesday to mark the 30th anniversary of the Alternative Energy Promotion Centre (AEPC), Shrestha stressed the need to link renewable energy projects, including solar power, micro-hydropower, biogas and biomass, with agriculture, industry and tourism. He also directed the AEPC to develop plans to make local governments free from dependence on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). Highlighting the centre’s achievements over the past three decades, Shrestha said more than 3.7 million households had benefited from its programmes. He emphasised the importance of decentralised energy systems in reducing vulnerability to climate-related disasters, particularly floods and extreme rainfall. Shrestha also described the proposed Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Bill as an important step towards strengthening the legal framework governing the sector. He called for greater mobilisation of international climate finance, carbon trading opportunities and technology partnerships to accelerate Nepal’s transition towards sustainable energy.

Nepal Oil Corporation reaches final handover stage of Rs 228.7 million ERP project

Nepal Oil Corporation (NOC) has reached the final handover stage of its Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system, nearly five and a half years after signing the initial contract for the digital transformation project. The system was developed by Neoteric Neo Software JV following a contract agreement signed around mid-2020. Valued at Rs 228.7 million, the project has received cumulative payments of Rs 194.1 million so far. The ERP platform integrates the corporation’s major operational functions, including administration, finance, procurement and inventory management. According to the project details, the system connects around 1,500 fuel dealers, 60 bottling plants and 60 airlines, enabling more integrated management of the corporation’s operations. The project also facilitates automated procurement-related coordination with Indian Oil Corporation. The system underwent independent evaluation by Uniconsult of Kathmandu University before reaching the final handover stage. The digital platform is expected to improve operational efficiency, strengthen institutional transparency and reduce manual processes across the corporation.

Infrastructure ministry moves to terminate six delayed construction contracts

The Ministry of Infrastructure Development has decided to terminate six long-delayed and underperforming construction contracts under the Department of Local Infrastructure. The decision was taken at a performance review meeting held on Wednesday to assess the progress of public infrastructure projects and address persistent implementation delays. According to the ministry, 19 stalled projects had been identified across regional divisions for review. Administrative action has been initiated against six contracts involving projects considered unlikely to be completed within the stipulated timeframe. Meanwhile, the ministry said six previously delayed infrastructure projects had been completed following closer monitoring and intervention. Construction work has also resumed at five other project sites where activities had previously come to a halt. The ministry further announced plans to revise operational guidelines for local infrastructure development to improve project implementation, strengthen monitoring and accelerate construction.

Health Insurance Board launches online portal for institutional enrolment

The Health Insurance Board has launched a digital platform, HIB E-Portal, to facilitate bulk enrolment and renewal of health insurance policies through provincial and local governments. The portal was initially introduced in collaboration with Gokarneshwor Municipality in Kathmandu and Kapilvastu Municipality in Kapilvastu. The new system is designed to replace time-consuming paper-based procedures and simplify the process of enrolling large groups of beneficiaries in the national health insurance programme. Through customised digital dashboards, local governments can upload beneficiary details, generate insurance membership cards and process premium payments online. The platform is also expected to eliminate the need for repeated visits to district-level administrative offices, reducing paperwork, processing time and administrative costs. The initiative is expected to make health insurance services more accessible and efficient, particularly for people living in remote areas.

Insurance Authority proposes new engineering insurance directive

The Nepal Insurance Authority has published a draft of the Engineering Insurance Directive, 2025, proposing standardised rules for risk assessment, premium determination and claims settlement in the engineering insurance sector. The proposed directive seeks to introduce mandatory site inspections and professional risk assessment reports for construction and erection insurance contracts with coverage exceeding Rs 10 million. It also proposes similar requirements for annual machinery insurance policies valued at more than Rs 1 million. The draft covers six categories of engineering insurance, including contractors’ all-risks insurance and machinery breakdown coverage. It also proposes standardised policy wordings, provisions for premium payments in instalments within a 60-day period and minimum premium rates. The authority said the proposed provisions are aimed at improving risk assessment, promoting transparency and ensuring consistency in insurance practices. The introduction of minimum premium rates is also intended to discourage unhealthy competition and excessive undercutting among insurance companies. The draft directive is expected to establish a more consistent regulatory framework for engineering insurance and strengthen policyholder protection.

Customs Department and Civil Aviation Authority introduce digital clearance system for aircraft imports

The Department of Customs and the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal have signed an agreement to simplify and digitise import and export clearance procedures for aircraft and aviation-related spare parts. The agreement, signed on Wednesday, provides for the integration of their services through the National Single Window system, allowing aviation operators to obtain required regulatory clearances and import recommendations online. The digital system will cover goods classified under customs tariff headings 8801 and 8802, which relate to aircraft and associated aviation equipment. The arrangement is expected to eliminate the need for physical paperwork and reduce delays caused by having to visit multiple government offices for regulatory approvals. The integration will also facilitate faster information sharing and coordination between the two agencies, improving transparency and efficiency in aviation-related trade procedures. The initiative is part of the government’s broader effort to expand digital public services and simplify trade-related administrative processes.

122 depositors receive refunds from seven troubled cooperatives

A total of 122 depositors of seven financially troubled cooperatives have received refunds through funds recovered from outstanding loans, according to the Problematic Cooperative Management Committee. Of the total beneficiaries, 23 depositors of Nepal Cooperative Financial Cooperative, Ideal Yamuna Hamro Multipurpose Cooperative and Shiv Shikhar Cooperative received full refunds. Meanwhile, 99 depositors of Kantipur Cooperative, Gautamshree Multipurpose Cooperative, Agriculture Development Multipurpose Cooperative and Shree Laligurans Multipurpose Cooperative received partial refunds. The committee said the payments were made using funds recovered from loans owed to the troubled cooperatives. It has prioritised depositors with relatively smaller savings as part of its initial refund process. According to the committee, the remaining refunds will be distributed in phases, with depositors categorised according to the amounts they had deposited. The recovery of outstanding loans and management of assets belonging to troubled cooperatives are continuing in accordance with existing laws to generate funds for repaying depositors.

Bhairahawa customs office exceeds quarterly revenue target by 13.86%

The Bhairahawa Customs Office collected Rs 33.34 billion in revenue during the first quarter of fiscal year 2026/27, exceeding its target by 13.86 percent. The office had set a revenue target of Rs 29.28 billion for the period ending October 1. Its actual collection was also 20.10 percent higher than the Rs 27.76 billion collected during the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. According to the chief customs officer, the increase in revenue was largely driven by higher imports of vehicles, particularly unassembled motorcycles and electric cars. He attributed the growth in imports partly to changes in supply routes following disruptions along northern trade corridors.

Tourism minister promotes Nepal at WTM London 2026

Minister for Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation Khadak Raj Paudel has held discussions with international counterparts and tourism representatives on expanding Nepal’s global tourism presence, improving air connectivity and attracting foreign investment. During his participation in the World Travel Market (WTM) 2026 in London, Paudel met tourism officials from India and the United Arab Emirates, as well as parliamentary representatives, to explore opportunities for greater cooperation. The minister highlighted Nepal’s potential in Himalayan adventure tourism, cultural heritage and wellness tourism, stressing the need to strengthen international partnerships to attract more visitors. The Nepali delegation also promoted preparations for Nepal Wellness Tourism Year 2027 and highlighted the country’s tourism attractions through the ‘Nepal is Open’ campaign. A total of 32 Nepali tourism enterprises are participating in the event at stall number N8-530, showcasing Nepal’s tourism products and services to international visitors. The delegation also sought to reassure prospective travellers about accessibility to major tourist destinations following recent flood-related disruptions.

Land revenue office employee arrested with Rs 100,000 bribe in Sarlahi

An employee of the Land Revenue Office in Sarlahi has been arrested on suspicion of accepting a Rs 100,000 bribe from a service seeker in exchange for facilitating a land-related administrative process. A team from the Bardibas office of the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) arrested Nirmal Timilsina, a non-gazetted first-class officer, from the office’s administration section at around 10 am on Wednesday. According to the CIAA, Timilsina allegedly accepted the money after promising to resolve an issue related to land tenancy rights. The commission confirmed the arrest and said further investigation into the alleged bribery was underway.

SEBON approves NIC Asia Bank’s Rs 7.46 billion rights share issue

The Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON) has approved NIC Asia Bank Limited’s proposal to issue rights shares equivalent to 50 percent of its existing paid-up capital. Under the approved plan, the bank will issue 74.58 million ordinary shares at a face value of Rs 100 each, raising approximately Rs 7.458 billion. The rights issue follows preliminary approval from Nepal Rastra Bank and is intended to strengthen the bank’s capital base and support its future business expansion. NIMB S Capital has been appointed as the issue manager for the offering. Eligible existing shareholders will be able to subscribe to the additional shares in accordance with the approved rights issue arrangements.

Nepal Reinsurance shares hit positive circuit limit after Cabinet approval

Shares of Nepal Reinsurance Company Limited surged 15 percent on Wednesday, hitting the positive circuit limit following the government’s decision to approve additional investment in the company through a rights share issue. The Cabinet meeting held on Tuesday, November 3, approved the government’s participation in the proposed rights share investment, boosting investor confidence in the company. Following the decision, the company’s share price increased by Rs 120.20 to close at Rs 921.70 on the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE). The sharp rise reflects positive market sentiment surrounding the proposed capital injection and its potential implications for the company’s financial position.

Three young entrepreneurs turn flower farming into business in Nepalgunj

Three young graduates have ventured into commercial floriculture in Nepalgunj, turning their agricultural interests into a promising business ahead of the Tihar festival. Ved Raj Acharya, Asim Sigdel and Chetan KC have established Fit Farm on 3,386 square metres of land at Phutaha in Ward No. 19 of Nepalgunj Sub-Metropolitan City. The trio began cultivation at the start of the current fiscal year using seeds brought from Chitwan. They selected suitable land and developed proper drainage facilities to minimise the risk of damage during the monsoon. The initiative has already generated flower sales worth around Rs 50,000, with advance bookings and retail orders received ahead of Tihar. The entrepreneurs have also received enquiries from Butwal, Dang, Kathmandu and Surkhet. They have been using social media platforms to promote their products and reach potential customers beyond the local market. The entrepreneurs plan to diversify their farming activities by adding watermelon and strawberry cultivation in the future. According to former Floriculture Association member Bindu Chharti Magar, commercial flower farming currently covers approximately 8.8 hectares, or 87,900 square metres, in Banke district. The growing interest among young entrepreneurs is expected to provide fresh momentum to commercial agriculture and create opportunities for local employment.

Tourism Department invites applications to upgrade small casino licences

The Department of Tourism has introduced simplified procedures allowing existing small-scale casino operators to upgrade their licences and expand their operations, subject to compliance with prescribed legal and regulatory requirements. Under the revised regulatory provisions, companies holding small casino licences can apply to upgrade to large-scale operations, expand their designated gaming areas or increase the number of gaming tables and electronic gaming machines. The department has invited eligible casino operators to submit applications through the prescribed administrative process. The revised arrangements are aimed at facilitating investment in the regulated entertainment and hospitality sector while ensuring that operators meet the necessary licensing standards. The department expects the changes to support the development of tourism-related businesses and strengthen regulatory compliance in the casino industry.

Tourism rebounds in Langtang and Gosaikunda after trail restoration

Tourism activities in Langtang and Gosaikunda have begun recovering following the restoration of roads and trekking trails damaged by the September 1 flash flood. The reopening of key transportation routes and trekking paths has encouraged domestic and international visitors to return to the popular Himalayan destinations during the autumn tourist season. According to the Langtang National Park conservation office, the construction of a Bailey bridge at Betrawati has restored an important transportation link, helping facilitate the movement of visitors. Tourism entrepreneurs have also reported an encouraging flow of tourists, with restored trails and the region’s scenic Himalayan landscapes attracting trekkers. The recovery of access routes is expected to provide a much-needed boost to tourism businesses and local livelihoods in Rasuwa, which were affected by the disaster.

CAAN forms five-member panel to probe helicopter collision in Solukhumbu

The Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN) has formed a five-member investigation committee to examine Tuesday’s collision between two helicopters at Pheriche in Solukhumbu district. An Air Dynasty helicopter bearing registration number 9N-AOD and a Fishtail Air helicopter registered as 9N-AJR collided at Pheriche, leaving one person dead and two pilots and a passenger injured. The investigation committee is coordinated by CAAN Director Prabhakar Chandra Mallik and includes pilots and aircraft engineers. The panel has been tasked with examining the circumstances surrounding the accident, identifying its immediate and underlying causes, and assessing the factors that may have contributed to the collision. It will submit a report containing recommendations aimed at preventing similar aviation accidents in the future.

title: Only one of seven Indian company projects is under construction in Nepal — Kathmandu Post - UA.NEWS
description: Only one of seven Indian company projects is under construction in Nepal — Kathmandu Post  UA.NEWS
publisher.title: UA.NEWS
full_article:
Of the seven major hydropower projects in Nepal with a total capacity of about 4,700 MW awarded to Indian state-owned and private companies, only one is under construction. This is the 900 MW Arun-III project in Sankhuwasabha district. As Kathmandu Post reports, the delays cast doubt on the country’s ability to implement plans to export electricity to India.

In January 2024, Nepal and India signed an agreement on exporting 10,000 MW of electricity over ten years. Nepal expects revenue from electricity supplies and a reduction in its trade deficit with India, which is the main buyer of Nepalese electricity.

The only active project

Construction of Arun-III began in 2018, but the initial five-year schedule has been revised repeatedly, including because of the Covid-19 pandemic. The generating component of the project is 77.5% complete, while the transmission line is 60% complete. Commercial generation was initially planned to begin by mid-April 2025, but the latest completion deadline has been moved to mid-March 2028.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

The project is being implemented by SJVN Arun-3 Power Development Company, a subsidiary of India’s state-owned SJVN Limited. Nepal is to receive 21.9% of the electricity generated by Arun-III free of charge, as well as royalties. A 253-kilometer, 400 kV transmission line is being built in parallel to connect the power plant with Sitamarhi in India.

Other projects and lines

Projects whose construction has not yet begun include the 900 MW Upper Karnali, the 679 MW Lower Arun, Arun-IV, West Seti, and Seti River-6. For Upper Karnali, Nepal’s Investment Board has accepted financing documents, allowing the project to move into the construction process. Negotiations on project development agreements are continuing for West Seti and Seti River-6.

Meanwhile, Nepal and India are expanding their cross-border power grid. Electricity imports and exports are already carried out through the Dhalkebar–Muzaffarpur line, while the under-construction Dhalkebar–Sitamarhi line is expected to provide export capacity of up to 1,650 MW. The Butwal–Gorakhpur line provides for a further up to 200 MW of exports.

full_article: Kathmandu. The Ministry of Health and Population has prepared a 'Concept Paper on Mental Health Bill' to ensure citizens' mental health rights. The bill is being drafted as the problem is becoming complex due to insufficient importance given to mental health, despite the Constitution of Nepal guaranteeing the right to health, equality, and living with dignity. The principle of drafting the bill was approved by the Council of Ministers meeting on October 19. In the context of Article 35(3) of the Constitution ensuring equal access to health services and Article 16 ensuring the right to live with dignity, the concept paper states that a law is essential to penalize negative behavior and stigma towards individuals with mental health problems. As health service delivery is a shared responsibility of the federal, provincial, and local levels, this specific federal law is necessary for the effective expansion, coordination, and regulation of mental health services. According to the Ministry of Health, the burden of mental health and psychosocial problems in Nepal is continuously increasing, with mental health accounting for approximately 15 percent of the total disease burden. Various study reports indicate that 7.2 percent of individuals in Nepal exhibit suicidal thoughts or behavior. According to the annual report of the Nepal Police for fiscal year 2080/81, 7,221 suicide-related incidents were registered across the country. Various studies have found self-harm to be among the top 10 causes of death in Nepal. Data shows that the mortality rate due to suicide has increased by 0.7 per hundred thousand population in the last decade. For this reason too, an act is necessary to formulate mental health programs. Nepal has an international obligation to fulfill commitments to international documents such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the Sustainable Development Goals, the Mental Health Action Plan (2013-2030), and the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities by formulating this law. Furthermore, the esteemed Supreme Court has issued mandamus and directive orders in various writ petitions to treat mentally ill prisoners, mandatorily allocate a certain percentage of the budget, and amend and revise discriminatory laws. The National Health Policy 2076, the policy and program and budget statement for fiscal year 2083/084, which the government has been advancing, consider mental health as an integral part of public health. Mental and psychosocial problems account for approximately 15 percent of the total disease burden in Nepal. It is estimated to cause an economic loss of about 0.44 percent of the gross domestic product. Similarly, the concept paper mentions that 78 percent of mental health patients are still outside the reach of treatment, and the increasing number of suicides clearly indicates the need for a new law. By studying India's 'Mental Healthcare Act 2017', Bangladesh's 'Mental Health Act 2018', and Thailand's 'Mental Health Act 2008', Nepal has moved forward with the process of enacting a modern and rights-oriented law. The concept paper states that for the implementation of the law, a separate mental health division or unit will be established at the federal level, and resources will be efficiently utilized through the strengthening and restructuring of existing structures and manpower. After the implementation of this act, it is expected that there will be uniformity in the understanding of mental health, multi-sectoral programs for suicide prevention will be strengthened, stigma and discrimination in society will decrease, and the human rights of persons with mental and psychosocial disabilities will be fully protected. The proposed bill will include comprehensive provisions related to mental health institutions, psychiatrists, emergency treatment, informed consent, supported decision-making systems, suicide prevention, reduction of childhood mental stress, and coordination between federal, provincial, and local levels. The concept paper states that for the implementation of the law, a separate mental health division or unit will be established at the federal level, and resources will be efficiently utilized through the strengthening and restructuring of existing structures and manpower. Through the implementation of this act, the goal is to bring uniformity in the understanding of mental health, promote the mental well-being of individuals, and enhance healthy lifestyles, productivity, and social participation. Furthermore, the mental health system will be strengthened, leading to its effective integration into primary healthcare, an effective referral system, and the expansion of quality services. The subject of expanding quality, accessible, and affordable treatment, care, and rehabilitation services, ensuring equal access to mental health services for all, has been included. The new system is expected to strengthen multi-sectoral programs for suicide prevention and bring a significant reduction in the suicide rate. It is mentioned that by reducing the stigma and discrimination towards mental illness in society, patients will be able to receive services easily, and an environment of cooperation will be strengthened in families, communities, and workplaces. After obtaining the opinion and consent from the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs and getting the principle approved by the Council of Ministers, the draft of the bill will be finalized in consultation and agreement with experts, stakeholders, the Ministry of Finance, and the Office of the Attorney General.

Social media statistics for Nepal in 2027

Proprietary analysis conducted by Manochi on behalf of DataReportal indicates that there were 15.0 million active social media user identities in Nepal in October 2026.

For perspective, this figure was equivalent to 50.6 percent of Nepal’s total population at the end of 2026.

However, while Manochi’s methodology strives to “de-duplicate” social media users across different social platforms — and, wherever possible, to remove accounts that do not represent individual human users — it’s important to stress that our social media user identities figures may not represent unique individuals (see our detailed notes on data to learn why).

Moreover, due to complexities associated with de-duplicating users across different social platforms, the methodology that we use to calculate social media user identities may sometimes only factor users of the social media platform that has the largest reported ad audience in the respective country at the time of report production.

As a result, the figures that we publish for a country’s overall social media use may sometimes look very similar to the statistics that we publish for the largest individual social media platform in that country.

Even in such cases, however, the potential audience reach values reported by individual social media platforms may exceed the values that we report for the total population, for the population in specific age groups, or for a country’s total internet user base.

We recognise that such anomalies may seem implausible, but — because these are figures reported by the platforms themselves — we’ve elected to publish values “as is”, because these anomalies may offer valuable insights in their own right (you can find more details in our extensive notes on data). These anomalies are one of the primary reasons why we refer to “social media user identities” instead of “social media users”.

Separately, please also note that the signals and sources that we rely on to inform these social media figures make regular changes and corrections to their data.

Consequently, the values for social media use shown here might appear to be quite different to the numbers that we published in previous years.

Because of this, we advise significant caution when comparing the values for social media user identities published in this year’s reports with those published in previous years, especially because changes in our reported values may be the result of “corrections” in the source data, and not all trends will be the result of changes in actual user behaviour.

title: Why Nepal are missing from the SAFF Championship 2026 - The Daily Star
description: Why Nepal are missing from the SAFF Championship 2026  The Daily Star
publisher.title: The Daily Star
full_article:
As the SAFF Championship 2026 kicks off in Dhaka on Thursday, the regional footballing fraternity will notice a glaring omission.

Nepal, traditionally one of South Asia's most passionate footballing nations, are entirely missing from the tournament bracket. This marks an unprecedented omission for the Himalayan nation who have never won the competition. Nepal have reached the final once, in 2021, but suffered a 3-0 defeat to India.

Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source

The absence has nothing to do with sporting merit, but rather a severe administrative crisis that has completely isolated the country from the international game.

Read more SAFF Championship around the corner, but no one seems ready

On June 24, world football's governing body, FIFA, handed a blanket suspension to the All Nepal Football Association (ANFA), citing third-party government and administrative interference in the federation's operations.

The suspension was the culmination of an escalating domestic crisis in Kathmandu. Nepal's Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) and other government bodies had launched aggressive probes into ANFA's financial dealings. Investigations surrounding jersey sales, ticketing irregularities, and murky administrative practices crossed FIFA's strict statutory red lines, which mandate that member federations must manage their affairs independently and without legal or political interference from their governments.

Despite the active ban, the South Asian Football Federation (SAFF) initially attempted to throw Nepal a lifeline. During the official tournament draw ceremony on August 1, organisers granted ANFA a two-month grace period to settle its internal disputes.

While Nepal were naturally excluded from the initial draw pots, SAFF declared that if the federation could appease FIFA and have the suspension lifted by September 30, the team would be parachuted directly into the group featuring host nation Bangladesh.

That two-month window came and went without a resolution. With the September 30 deadline officially missed, the door was firmly shut on Nepal's participation in the 15th edition of the regional showpiece.

The fallout extends far beyond just the SAFF Championship. Under the ongoing FIFA and Asian Football Confederation (AFC) sanctions, Nepal's national teams and domestic clubs remain strictly barred from all official international competitions.

title: Nepali Congress calls informal meeting amid political tensions - Khabarhub

full_article:
KATHMANDU: The Nepali Congress (NC), the main opposition party, is holding an informal meeting of its office-bearers today to discuss recent political developments and key organisational issues.

The meeting is scheduled to take place at 3 pm at the party’s central office in Sanepa. A party leader said the discussions would focus on the latest political developments, including the government’s decision to remove Dan Bahadur Karki from the post of Inspector General of Police (IGP) and appoint Manoj Karki as his successor.

Meanwhile, controversy has also emerged over allegations that NC President Gagan Thapa spent Rs. 180 million to secure the party’s legal status. The Nepali Congress has dismissed the allegations as a government conspiracy, claiming that the government is attempting to question the party’s legitimacy through baseless and fabricated accusations.

The party has said it will challenge what it describes as attempts to suppress the opposition’s voice through both political and legal means. It has also expressed opposition to interference in judicial independence and press freedom.

The Nepali Congress has further demanded the formation of a parliamentary investigation committee to look into the government’s recent controversial activities, including the arrest of journalists.

title: Nepali Congress President Thapa asks Oli to save government — Kathmandu Post - UA.NEWS
description: Nepali Congress President Thapa asks Oli to save government — Kathmandu Post  UA.NEWS
publisher.title: UA.NEWS
full_article:
In Nepal, Nepali Congress President Gagan Thapa held talks with CPN-UML chair K. P. Sharma Oli in an effort to save his party’s government in Madhesh Province. The head of the provincial government, Krishna Prasad Yadav, must seek a vote of confidence after CPN-UML withdrew its support for the coalition, the Kathmandu Post reports.

Coalition talks

According to the publication’s sources, Thapa met Oli at his residence in Gundu, Bhaktapur District, on Tuesday evening. He said that changing the provincial government a year before the assembly’s term ends would send a negative signal and called for the coalition to be restored.

On October 16, CPN-UML withdrew its support for Yadav’s cabinet and recalled its four ministers. The party accused the Nepali Congress-led coalition of failing to implement a 15-point agreement. Yadav must secure a vote of confidence within 30 days.

Birendra Singh, vice president of the Nepali Congress in Madhesh and a member of the provincial assembly, said the party is discussing the vote of confidence with all political forces, but no specific decision has yet been made.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

Attempts to form another majority

According to sources, Oli told Thapa that he would hold consultations with the leaders of the Nepal Communist Party and CPN-UML. The Nepal Communist Party continues to support Yadav, although it cooperates with CPN-UML in other provinces.

CPN-UML also considered forming a new government together with JSP Nepal, the Janamat party, and the Nepal Communist Party. The talks stalled because JSP Nepal chair Upendra Yadav and Janamat chair C. K. Raut did not support the plan.

In the 104-seat provincial assembly, JSP Nepal has 28 lawmakers, CPN-UML has 24, the Nepali Congress has 22, the Nepal Communist Party has 15, and Janamat has 12. A majority requires 53 votes, so Yadav will need support beyond the Nepali Congress if CPN-UML votes against him.

title: Can Nepal’s Jobs and Care Agenda Deliver Stronger Businesses and More Secure Family Incomes? - Devdiscourse
description: Can Nepal’s Jobs and Care Agenda Deliver Stronger Businesses and More Secure Family Incomes?  Devdiscourse
publisher.title: Devdiscourse
full_article:
Nepal's effort to connect employment, social protection and care services could influence how small businesses recruit workers, how families manage essential expenses and how governments support economic growth. The National Planning Commission and the Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment, supported by the International Labour Organization and UN Women, brought stakeholders together in Nagarkot on October 30–31, 2026, to advance this agenda. Discussions covered a national jobs and social protection roadmap and proposed employment and care economy policies.

For Nepal's traders and consumers, the significance lies in whether these proposals translate into accessible services and affordable protection. Better training could help enterprises find suitable workers, while stronger care services could allow more people to earn incomes. However, the workshop represents progress in policy preparation; it does not establish new benefits, guaranteed jobs or immediate financial assistance.

Better Skills Could Strengthen Nepal's Small Businesses

Agriculture, tourism, construction, the care economy and information and communication technology were identified as priority sectors for employment growth. Participants also recommended stronger coordination across government levels, implementation of the National Qualifications Framework, improved skills testing and a digital database connecting training providers and skilled workers.

For traders, these measures could address a practical problem: finding employees whose skills match business needs. Agricultural traders depend on reliable handling and distribution, tourism enterprises need consistent service, and construction suppliers benefit when projects have capable workers. Training linked to actual vacancies could improve productivity across these connected activities.

Yet training alone cannot create demand for labour. Policymakers will need employers involved in course design and should assess whether graduates secure suitable employment. Counting certificates without tracking job placement, earnings and employer satisfaction would provide an incomplete picture of success.

Consumers could benefit through more reliable services and better workmanship. Such gains would depend on training quality and business competition; improved skills would not automatically produce lower prices.

Social Protection Must Fit Irregular Incomes

Workshop recommendations included adapting contributory social security arrangements for workers in micro and small enterprises, temporary employment and part-time jobs. Participants also discussed stronger support for vulnerable groups and integrated digital services covering registration, employment information and social security enrolment.

This matters for small traders whose earnings fluctuate. A contribution schedule designed around predictable monthly wages may be difficult for seasonal businesses and workers with interrupted employment. Flexible payment arrangements and clear benefit information could make participation more practical.

For consumers, stronger protection could help households maintain essential spending when earnings fall. More stable purchasing power could also support neighbourhood shops and service providers. These are potential economic effects, rather than outcomes demonstrated by the workshop.

The policy challenge is balancing affordability with sustainable financing. Contributions that businesses struggle to pay could discourage participation, while inadequate funding could undermine promised protection. Before implementation, workers and employers will need clarity about eligibility, payment obligations, benefits and complaint procedures.

Digital integration could simplify administration, but assisted enrolment will remain important for people who struggle with online services. Registration should lead to usable protection, with straightforward procedures for claiming benefits.

Care Services Could Unlock Work and Consumer Demand

Care is becoming an economic planning issue as well as a household responsibility. The workshop account cites a projection that Nepal's population aged 60 and above will exceed 7.1 million by 2051, alongside continuing migration that could increase demand for support services.

For women managing substantial unpaid care responsibilities, accessible childcare and eldercare could make paid employment or business ownership more feasible. Traders could gain both potential employees and customers as households have greater freedom to participate in economic activity.

An expanding care sector could also create opportunities for service providers, training organisations and suppliers. However, growth must be accompanied by standards protecting care recipients and workers. Poorly regulated provision could expose families to unreliable services and employees to insecure conditions.

Affordability will determine who benefits. Policymakers should examine how public provision, community services and private providers can serve households with different incomes, including communities where commercial care services may struggle to operate.

The Policy Deadline Needs Budgets and Accountability

The government's stated ambition is to finalise the two proposed policies within the next 100 working days. That is a policy formulation target, rather than a deadline for delivering nationwide services or achieving employment outcomes.

For policymakers, credible implementation requires assigned responsibilities, realistic budgets and coordination between federal, provincial and local institutions. For traders, predictable rules and simple procedures will matter more than broad promises. Consumers will judge reforms through service availability, affordability and reliability.

Nepal should therefore connect policy commitments to measurable results: sustained employment, effective social protection coverage, accessible care and reduced administrative burdens. The opportunity is to reinforce household security and enterprise growth together. Delivery will depend on turning workshop recommendations into financed programmes that people can use.

title: Saudi firm to pay family of Nepali worker killed in drone attack - UA.NEWS
description: Saudi firm to pay family of Nepali worker killed in drone attack  UA.NEWS
publisher.title: UA.NEWS
full_article:
In Saudi Arabia, a company has agreed to pay 181,000 Saudi riyals to the family of 45-year-old Nepali worker Bharat Mahato, who was killed in a drone attack on the Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province. The amount includes 31,000 riyals in end-of-service benefits and 150,000 riyals in compensation.

Compensation after embassy appeal

The agreement was reached with the assistance of the Embassy of Nepal in Riyadh, Kathmandu Post reports. Kabiraj Upreti, the embassy's labour counsellor, said the funds would be transferred to the family after the necessary administrative procedures are completed.

Mahato worked as a cleaner on a Saudi Aramco project through Abdul Wahab Mansour Al Moallam Sons Company. His work permit had expired about a year before his death. As a result, the family could not claim support from Nepal's Foreign Employment Board or a payment under the insurance scheme for migrant workers.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

According to the publication, after the embassy informed the employer about the family's situation, the company decided to provide compensation from its own funds. Under Nepal's migrant worker support system, the family of a worker who dies abroad with a valid work permit can receive 1 million Nepalese rupees from the welfare fund and up to 1.5 million rupees under the term life insurance programme.

Death at the oil field

Bharat Mahato, a native of Nepal's Mahottari district, was killed on October 21. According to Kathmandu Post, the attack on the oil project was carried out by Yemen's Houthis; a worker from the Philippines was also killed. The Nepali embassy completed the procedures to repatriate Mahato's body, but disruptions to air travel are making it difficult to determine the date of its delivery to Nepal.

Mahato had worked in Saudi Arabia for 14 years and was his family's main breadwinner. After his death, his wife Indrika was left with four children and a loan for the construction of a house, which the family had been paying off with remittances from Saudi Arabia.

title: India and Nepal discuss agenda for Shah’s visit — Kathmandu Post - UA.NEWS
description: India and Nepal discuss agenda for Shah’s visit — Kathmandu Post  UA.NEWS
publisher.title: UA.NEWS
full_article:
In Kathmandu, Nepal, Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri held talks with senior officials of the country on the potential agenda for Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s upcoming visit to India. As Kathmandu Post reports, Misri arrived in the Nepali capital for a two-day visit at the invitation of his counterpart Amrit Bahadur Rai.

The Indian diplomat separately met with Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and other government officials. Later, he held delegation-level talks with Rai. Nepal’s Foreign Ministry said the sides discussed exchanges of high-level visits, transport connectivity, trade, development cooperation, energy and people-to-people contacts.

Possible dates of the trip

The official dates of Shah’s visit to India have not yet been announced. According to the newspaper’s sources, November 22–25 is being named as a possible period. The trip is expected to last three days, and the Nepali prime minister will not travel outside New Delhi. There, he is expected to hold talks with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and meet with other senior officials.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

On Thursday, Misri is to meet with Shah and deliver him an invitation from Modi. If the trip takes place, it will be Shah’s first official bilateral foreign trip since taking office on March 27.

Assistance and joint projects

The meetings also covered financial assistance to Nepal, trade, transit, border issues, energy, and the development of transport and digital infrastructure. Nepal is asking India to provide more than $2 billion in the form of lines of credit, grants and other economic assistance to restore infrastructure damaged by floods in Bhotekoshi. The requested components include a $1 billion line of credit, $500 million in grants and another $500 million for reconstruction.

During Shah’s visit, the prime ministers of the two countries are expected to be able to inaugurate several facilities completed with India’s support. These include the Nepal Police Academy in Panauti, a bridge in Darchula, an integrated border post in Bhairahawa and a road bridge across the Mahakali River. The sides may also jointly begin construction of an integrated border post in Dodhara-Chandani, the Lower Arun hydropower project and an oil pipeline from India’s Siliguri to Charali in Jhapa.

title: Nepalese tennis player Bastola receives wildcard for Australian Open qualifying — Kathmandu Post - UA.NEWS
description: Nepalese tennis player Bastola receives wildcard for Australian Open qualifying — Kathmandu Post  UA.NEWS
publisher.title: UA.NEWS
full_article:
Nepalese tennis player Abhishek Bastola will compete in the Australian Open 2027 Asia-Pacific Wildcard Playoff, to be held from November 23 to 28 in Chengdu, China. He received one of four wildcards for the qualifying round, Kathmandu Post reports.

Qualifying in Chengdu

Bastola will compete in singles. Eight participants will play in the qualifying round, with the top four advancing to the main draw, where 12 seeded players will await them.

Representatives of the Asia-Pacific region, excluding Australians, with a world ranking of 105+ are eligible for the playoff. The winners of the singles and doubles competitions will be included in the Australian Open entry list.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

Nepal’s first representative

Bastola, who represented Nepal at four Asian Games, will become the first Nepalese player at this tournament. At a press conference, the tennis player said he had long dreamed of playing at the Australian Open and would make every effort in the competition.

At the same time, Bastola said that he had not received adequate support either from the state or from the tennis association.

title: Traffic opens on bridge over Lalbakaiya in Nepal after 12 years — Kathmandu Post - UA.NEWS
description: Traffic opens on bridge over Lalbakaiya in Nepal after 12 years — Kathmandu Post  UA.NEWS
publisher.title: UA.NEWS
full_article:
In Nepal, vehicles have begun crossing the Tikulia bridge over the Lalbakaiya River in Rautahat District, whose construction lasted 12 years. The bridge is expected to make it easier for residents of the Gaur and Ishnath municipalities to access fields, hospitals and the district administrative center.

As the Kathmandu Post reports, construction work is nearly complete. Arun Kumar Lal Karna, head of the road office in Chandranigahapur, said that an access road still needs to be built and river channel reinforcement work carried out.

A crossing instead of dangerous boats

For residents of the villages of Banjharaha, Auriya and Mathiya, the bridge is expected to simplify travel to Gaur. Residents of Tikulia, whose agricultural land is located on the other side of the Lalbakaiya, will be able to avoid dangerous daily trips to their fields.

During the monsoon season, rising water levels made boat transport especially dangerous and complicated the transportation of patients to hospitals and farmers’ access to fields. On August 25, 2017, a boat carrying 29 people returning from agricultural work lost control in a strong current, collided with a support of the unfinished bridge and capsized. Twenty-four passengers were rescued, while five died.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

Delays and a contractor change

The foundation of the concrete bridge was laid in July 2014 with the participation of then Prime Minister Sushil Koirala. Pappu Construction was to complete the project by July 2018 for 149.327 million Nepalese rupees, but by 2017 it had completed only 17% of the work.

The Department of Roads blacklisted Pappu Construction and terminated the contract in June 2023. In September of the same year, a new contract worth 276.6 million Nepalese rupees was awarded to the Azad Dipu JV Rautahat joint venture. Its representative, Ramsagar Raut, said the project had been made operational, although river channel reinforcement is delayed because of a shortage of stones.

Gaur Mayor Shambhu Sah noted that the bridge, which could have been built in three to four years, took 12 years to construct.

title: Nearly 10 million Nepali children exposed to unhealthy air, UNICEF warns - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nearly 10 million Nepali children exposed to unhealthy air, UNICEF warns  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nearly 10 million children in Nepal are exposed to unhealthy levels of air pollution, while millions more face risks from drought, extreme heat and landslides, according to a new UNICEF report highlighting the growing toll of climate change and environmental hazards on children's lives.

The advocacy brief, Growing Up in a Climate Hotspot: The Risks Shaping the Lives and Futures of Nepal's Children , draws on national and global data to show how climate change, pollution and disasters are threatening children's health, nutrition, education and protection. It calls for children's rights and needs to be placed at the centre of climate policies, financing and action.

The findings show that 9.9 million children are exposed to unhealthy air pollution, 7.3 million to drought and 5.7 million to extreme hot days. Another 2.9 million face exposure to rainfall-triggered landslides, while an estimated 2.4 million are exposed to multiple high-intensity climate hazards, compounding their risks and making recovery harder.

Beyond direct exposure to hazards, climate change is putting growing pressure on essential services that children depend on, the report says.

Despite Nepal's development gains, only 47.5 percent of the population has access to safely managed drinking water. One in four children under five is stunted, while 22 percent of children live in multidimensional poverty. Climate-related shocks are also increasing the risks of child labour, child marriage, disease outbreaks and disruption to education.

“The climate crisis is increasingly becoming a child rights crisis,” said Alice Akunga, UNICEF representative to Nepal.

“Children have contributed least to climate change, yet they are among those bearing its greatest consequences. Every flood, drought, heatwave and pollution episode threatens children's health, nutrition, education and protection,” she said.

With Nepal preparing to participate in global climate discussions at COP31, Akunga said the country had an opportunity and responsibility to put children at the centre of climate action, financing and adaptation.

The risks are not evenly distributed. Children living in poverty, girls, those with disabilities, children from historically marginalised communities and those in remote, climate-vulnerable areas face disproportionately high risks and have fewer resources to cope with and recover from disasters.

In a step towards more child- and youth-responsive climate action, the government endorsed the Declaration on Children, Youth and Climate Action at the National Climate Summit on October 29.

Launched at COP25, the first-of-its-kind global declaration has been endorsed by 78 countries. It commits governments to climate action that recognises the rights, needs and contributions of children and young people.

The endorsement builds on Nepal's global recognition for having one of the world's most child-responsive climate plans. The signed declaration will be formally handed over to UNICEF representatives at COP31 in Türkiye.

Ahead of the summit, UNICEF Nepal has urged the government to integrate children's rights and needs into climate policies, adaptation plans, disaster risk reduction strategies and climate financing.

It has also called on governments, development partners and climate finance institutions to increase investment in child-responsive adaptation and loss and damage, particularly in resilient health, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene, education, child protection and social protection services. Access to these services should take account of age, gender and disability.

The agency has further urged national and subnational governments to use disaggregated, child-focused climate risk data to guide planning and prioritise vulnerable communities. It wants the private sector to invest in climate-resilient infrastructure, clean energy and innovations that protect children's wellbeing.

UNICEF has also called on all stakeholders to ensure children and young people have meaningful roles in climate decision-making at local, national and global levels.

The report stresses the importance of listening to young people, who are already leading local climate initiatives and advocating stronger action.

“Climate change is not a future problem for children; it is already affecting our lives today,” said Jayanti Bam, UNICEF Nepal Youth Advocate for Climate Action.
